subject: Uptick synchronization and gradeband cohorting for multi-year term
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial proposal: synchronized uptick + gradeband cohorting for 3yr term

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass structure that matches what we discussed: a 3-year term with an annual graded uplift (gradebands) tied to usage cohorts, an auto-renew opt-in at year 2 with a mutually agreed notice window, and an escrowed credit buffer for the first 9 months to smooth onboarding spikes.

Key points in the attached matrix (redwood-pricing-gradebands-v3.xlsx):
- Year 1: low cohort (baseline) + 25% ramp allowance; credits held in escrow to cover onboarding surges.
- Year 2: cohort re-evaluation and potential grade shift if sustained +40% uptake.
- Year 3: stabilization; auto-renew clause triggers if both parties sign off 60 days prior.

Open questions for your ops/legal teams:
1) Is the 60-day auto-renew notice window acceptable?
2) Any regulatory constraints on holding the escrow credits (we can integrate with your finance team or use a third-party escrow).

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct I’ll loop in Marissa to draft the MAP language and Camila to run capacity checks for the proposed gradebands.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Lead Account Executive
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-pricing-gradebands-v3.xlsx (Excel worksheet, 1.2 MB)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightwellhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: synchronized uptick + gradeband cohorting for 3yr term

Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. High level this looks promising. A few clarifications from ops/legal before we go to MAP: 
- Escrow: we prefer a time-limited escrow (9 months is fine) but need to confirm whether Redwood can provide quarterly release reports.
- Auto-renew: 60 days is ok but can we add a hard cap on year-over-year price uplift (max 8% per year) that applies only if Redwood increases list pricing?
- Cohort re-eval: can you define the exact usage windows and metrics you’ll use to move customers between gradebands? We need deterministic thresholds.

If you can add those items into the MAP draft we’ll review with procurement next week.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Director of Cloud Ops, Brightwell Health
Daniel.Park@brightwellhealth.com

Quoted text follows:
> On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 9:12 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> > Thanks again for taking the time yesterday...
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-07T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: synchronized uptick + gradeband cohorting for 3yr term

Daniel —

Great notes — we can accommodate all three. Summary of updates I asked the team to prepare: 
- Escrow reporting cadence: quarterly release reports + monthly usage deltas for the first 9 months (we will provide a CSV export and a statement of funds released).
- Price uplift cap: we will add an explicit clause limiting Redwood-initiated list price increases to a maximum of 8% YoY for this agreement; marketplace surcharges/taxes excluded.
- Cohort thresholds: Camila is drafting deterministic thresholds (tokens/month brackets + 7‑day moving average) that will live in Appendix B; movement between gradebands requires sustained 60-day exceedance of the next bracket.

Marissa — can you draft the MAP language for these three items and include a short definition of 'sustained exceedance' language?
Camila — please validate we can guarantee the capacity curve assumptions for the gradebands and call out any warm-up times or pre-warming we recommend.

If we align on language by Friday, I’ll send a redline-ready MAP for procurement.

Best,
Lauren

Attachment: MAP-draft-2027.pdf (PDF, 340 KB)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-04-08T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial proposal: synchronized uptick + gradeband cohorting for 3yr term

Thanks — I dropped a draft MAP (section snippets below) into the shared draft and updated Appendix B language. Highlights: 
- Escrow schedule: quarterly releases tied to certified usage exports; escrow funds forfeited only after confirmed invoice reconciliation.
- Price cap: added clause 4.3.2 limiting Redwood list increases to max 8% YoY for the term (exceptions for mandatory regulatory fees called out).
- Gradeband movement: Appendix B now reads: "Gradeband movement requires a 60-day continuous exceedance of the next usage bracket measured by tokens/month with weekly sampling and a 7-day rolling average".

Camila: flagged two operational items in the comments — 1) a 48‑hour pre-warm for burst windows beyond +200% and 2) recommended a 1.5x staging buffer for month 0 onboarding to avoid throttling during cutover.

Daniel / Brightwell Ops: once you confirm the escrow approach and the 8% cap is acceptable, we can convert this to a redline-ready MAP and push to DocuSign. If you want, I can include a short summary page that calls out the operational guardrails and a simple waterfall showing when gradeband shifts would occur.

- Marissa
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment references: MAP-draft-2027.pdf (see section snippets in comments), redwood-pricing-gradebands-v3.xlsx
